text:
oliver: heads up — saw a spike in  p50 latency on the rocm pools this afternoon. digging into traces now but it looks like a bunch of requests are taking the generic_fallback_kernel path for seqlen=1024 on gfx1030.

maya: yikes. any obvious error in the router logs?

oliver: pasted a snippet from the router: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] route_decision: model=redwood-13b, gpu=gfx1030, requested_kernel=seqlen_1024_opt, available_kernels=[seqlen_512_opt,seqlen_2048_opt], decision=soft_reroute->generic_fallback_kernel, reason=missing_exact_seqlen
```

oliver: the autotune table doesn't list seqlen_1024 optimized kernels for gfx1030 (weird because we've had ones for 512 and 2048). latency jumps from ~60ms/token to ~200ms/token for those flows.

kevin: hmm that sounds like an autotuner catalog hole. did the offline autotune run for gfx1030 finish without errors? last run was 2026-03-10 I think.

maya: i pulled the autotune DB row: 
```
model: redwood-13b
arch: gfx1030
seqlens: [128,256,512,2048]
best_kernels: {...}
```
so 1024 is indeed missing. not sure why the autotuner skipped it.

sara: also seeing a correlation with KV cache miss patterns — long conversational traces churn the kv cache and bump memory pressure which causes the kernel selector to prefer the generic path (it has lower tmp memory footprint). profiler shows 2x more memcpy and a 30% reduction in kv_hit_rate.

rahul: interesting — so there are two effects: autotune catalog missing the optimized 1024 kernel AND runtime choosing generic fallback due to transient memory heuristics. we should fix both but prioritize the runtime guard so we don't take a 3x latency hit.

kevin: proposed short-term fixes: 
1) add a conditional in router: if seqlen in (768..1536) and arch==gfx1030 and batch_size<=4 then prefer nearest_smaller_kernel (512) over generic_fallback_kernel.
2) schedule an immediate autotune pass for 1024 on gfx1030.

oliver: +1 on (1). we saw many requests with bs=1..2; mapping 1024->512 opt kernel gives better perf than generic fallback in our offline microbench.

maya: careful — mapping 1024->512 requires kv-cache offset handling (kv indices differ) and we must ensure the kv-shift logic uses the right prefix lengths. failing that will corrupt attention states.

kevin: agree. implementation note: router should add a sticky flag "compatible_kernel_mapping" and the serving runtime should perform a lightweight validation step: compute expected kv_offset = (seq_len - mapped_seq_len) and if kv_offset % block_size==0 then allow mapping, else reject. cheap check.

sara: added perf numbers from local repro: 
```
request: seqlen=1024, bs=1, model=redwood-13b, gfx1030
- generic_fallback_kernel: p50=195ms/token, p95=310ms/token
- map_to_seqlen_512_opt: p50=72ms/token, p95=110ms/token
- ideal_seqlen_1024_opt (simulated): p50=68ms/token
```

oliver: big win. do we have any risk of quality/regression due to quantization differences in the 512 kernel path?

kevin: mapping to 512_opt does change how attention is chunked but since it's just kernel layout, the model outputs are bit-identical if we keep same dtype and numeric path. we should add an eval prompt set to compare outputs for a few cases though.

maya: i'm worried about the autotune skip root cause. autotune logs show timeouts for some benchmarks on gfx1030 around 1024 step (OOMs that then got retried and skipped). maybe an infra flake. I'll re-run with higher mem limits and longer timeouts.

rahul: operational plan: 
- maya: kick autotune run for gfx1030@1024 (high priority) — ETA 24h
- kevin: PR router guard + lightweight kv_offset check (canary to 5% traffic) — ETA 48h
- sara: create perf/regression eval comparing mapped_512 vs ideal_1024 on standard prompt set, include kv-heavy chat scenarios — ETA 48h
- oliver: monitor and roll back path, add alert if p95>200ms/token for rocm pools — ETA immediate

ci-bot: deploy request queued: builds/rocm-router/patch-389 -> staged canary 5% at 2026-03-16T02:00:00Z

oliver: thanks. note: also add a metric for "router_mapping_rate" so we can measure how often fallbacks are being mapped vs generic. low overhead.

kevin: one more thought — batching heuristics: if incoming traffic has variable seq lengths, our batcher sometimes pads to the longest seqlen in the batch and then the kernel selector sees the batch seqlen and picks generic. we should prefer bucketing by seqlen windows (128/256/512/1024/2048) before kernel selection. small change in batching, big perf gains.

maya: agreed. i'll prototype a bucketed batcher that groups within seqlen windows and emits batches that map cleanly to autotune entries.

sara: also include KV cache watermarking: avoid evicting mid-request; if memory pressure triggers during an active request, prefer shedding new batches rather than switching kernels.

oliver: good. assigning owners here: maya (autotune), kevin (router + mapping guard), sara (perf eval + batcher prototype), rahul (observability + alerts). i'll open a follow-up thread with links to the PRs and autotune job id.

maya: will do. thanks team :thumbsup:

kevin: i'll draft the router PR now and add unit tests for the kv_offset gate.

ci-bot: autotune job created: autotune-824519 (queued)

oliver: closing loop — once autotune finishes, if we have a native 1024 kernel we'll prefer it, otherwise keep the mapping guard. moving to action items.
